Who Is On Your Bills Viewing Favorite Mount Rushmore
stories.summary:
I was thinking about this recently on who would be my top four players that I just enjoyed watching play that would be my mount rushmore and figured it would be a fun exercise for us all.



	 



	A few caveats before I start.



	 



	Josh Allen/Jim Kelly are so obvious that I am not adding them because it would go without saying. So throw them some love if you want before you put your four but figure they are the sky of the mountain. You can't miss them lol. I started watching football in the mid 90s with my dad but wasn't until 98-99 era I got into it for real. If you saw them before that go for it! ... but maybe detail who they are for those of us who did not see them. This is your list so do what you want, this is not a who are the best four Bills ever.



	 



	My four favorite Bills to watch play:



	 



	1. Doug Flutie- I said I was 98-99 when it hit football max and he was such a big part of it. He was never the best player but the guy was a blast to watch and provided some truly fun moments for a bit there.



	2. Robert Woods- Legitimately sucks he left right before the team got good as he was such a good all around WR whether it was blocking guys or his ability to make some big catches. He was a guy I always wished got to play with Josh because of his skill set and what he could've done. Instead we have videos throwing his hands in the air as EJ air mailed it 15 yards over head lol



	3. Shady McCoy- Blue chip player who could make soo many great plays single handedly ... while also terrifying you the way he held the ball. He holds a special place for me as he got traded and paid but legitimately matched it with his play. 2017 he had 10 game with over 100 yards combined and he was a very big role on an offense that was not super good in helping them break the drought. His ability to hit a HR play though really was a pleasure to watch.



	4. Micah Hyde- The amount of times he came out of nowhere to break up a pass or create a turnover was so cool. I was thrilled when they signed him from Green Bay as he felt like a really good fit for the defense, but I'd be lying if I said I expected what came. He had many great moments and play once he arrived and it is a shame that neck injury seemed to end a career that had more years left to it.

New parking and tailgating rules at Highmark Stadium
stories.summary:
@Kirby Jackson mentioned this in the folding table topic and I think it probably deserves it's own topic so that event attendees are clear on the new rules.



	 



	https://www.buffalobills.com/stadium/parking



	 



	 



	Parking Code of Conduct



	To maintain a safe and family friendly environment, the Buffalo Bills ask that all guests adhere to the Parking Code of Conduct.  All guests must follow instructions of stadium personnel, and the following behaviors will not be tolerated. Violations of this Code of Conduct may result in ejection, arrest, and/or revocation of parking and ticket purchasing privileges.



	Behavior that is unruly, disruptive, or illegal in nature.



	Conduct that endangers spectators, Team Members, or participants.



	Inappropriate displays of affection for a public setting.



	Fighting, taunting, and threatening remarks or offensive gestures toward any fans including visiting team fans, as well as Highmark Stadium Team Members.



	Indecent exposure or undressing.



	Intoxication, binge drinking, or other signs of alcohol or substance impairment that result in irresponsible behavior.



	Scalping or other improper resale of tickets.



	Unauthorized solicitation and/or selling of any merchandise without the permission of the Buffalo Bills.



	Use of foul, disruptive, obscene, offensive, or abusive language or actions.



	Wearing obscene, offensive, political in nature, or indecent clothing.



	Displaying obscene, offensive, political in nature, or indecent signage, or flags.



	Any other behavior deemed dangerous or inappropriate by management.



	 



	Parking Policies



	All Highmark Stadium parking lots require an advanced purchase parking pass. Event Day parking transactions are limited to accessible parking only. See Accessible Parking for more information.



	Advanced purchase parking passes are valid for the parking lot designated on the pass only, and cannot be utilized to park in a different parking lot on the Highmark Stadium campus.



	Parking lots open (4) hours prior to kickoff and close (2) hours after the game concludes. Parking lot hours for concerts and other major events vary and are communicated via the Highmark Stadium website and social media.



	Abbott Road will be closed to all vehicle traffic (5) hours prior to kickoff between Bills Drive and the NFTA Transportation Hub on game days.



	Big Tree Road (Route 20A) will be closed to westbound traffic during postgame ONLY from Fieldhouse Drive to Route 219 and eastbound traffic during postgame ONLY from Erie College Drive to Southwestern Blvd.



	All guests must have a valid parking permit to park in a designated parking lot. Permits are valid for All guests parking in Highmark Stadium lots must also have a valid event ticket or credential.



	To ensure safe and efficient travel throughout Highmark Stadium parking lots and surrounding roads, please follow the directions of Erie County Sheriff Traffic, Security, and/or Premium Parking Staff.



	Parking spaces are not pre-assigned unless otherwise posted. Guests cannot choose their parking space, and will be directed to their parking location by Highmark Stadium parking staff. Reserving spaces is NOT permitted.



	The parking pass allows for one space per vehicle only. One car, one space.



	Refunds will not be made for lost, stolen, or unused parking passes. A refund or credit will be made only for event cancellations.



	Box trucks are prohibited, and vehicles may not enter the Stadium with anything in-tow (e.g., grills, trailers, etc.).



	Advertising or commercial activities; guest vehicles with exterior advertisement (e.g. wraps) are not allowed in the parking lot areas even with a valid parking pass. No commercial advertisement hung or displayed on guest vehicles, tents, signs, or by any other means possible is permitted.



	 



	Handicapped Accessible Lots



	Designated Accessible Parking Lots are Blue ADA and White ADA. Parking in both lots is on a first-come, first-served basis. All payments are cashless and must be made upon arrival. There are no advanced permits sold to these parking lots.



	Parking on adjacent roads and streets to wait for ADA Parking Lots to open is strictly prohibited. Violators are subject to being ticketed and/or towed by the Erie County Sheriff's Department & Orchard Park Police.



	Accessible parking is also available for valid pass holders in the Bronze, Gold, & Platinum lots. Limited accessible parking overflow is available in other parking lots and will be managed on a case-by-case basis by our parking team.



	Proper permits are required to park in accessible spaces. Parking placards for guests with disabilities are available through state or town government offices.



	Vehicles parked in accessible parking spaces without the proper legal parking placards are subject to be towed and/or fined.



	All tailgating activity must fit within designated ADA parking space striping. Tailgating is strictly prohibited at all times within the crosshatched ADA access aisles located between designated ADA spaces.



	The Buffalo Bills Guest Experience team provides ADA golf cart transportation from Bills parking lots to stadium gates for fans in need. For more information, see the ADA Pick Up/Drop Off map, or on Game Day call the Game Day Fan Hotline at 716-312-8933.



	 



	Bus & Limo Lot



	Parking permits must be purchased in advance of Bills home games through the Buffalo Bills Ticket Office. Buses or limos that show up on game day without a parking permit will not be permitted entry.



	There is no tailgating or loitering permitted next to or around parked buses. Tailgating in the Bus & Limo Lot is only permitted for limousines with a capacity of 11 persons or fewer.



	Sprinter Vans of any size will be parked in the Limo Lot and must purchase a parking pass in advance. Sprinter vans will not be permitted to park in the Blue, Bronze, Gold, Green, Grey, Orange, Platinum or White lots.



	Buses & Limos are not permitted to depart the Bus & Limo Lot on the day of a game until (1) hour after the game has concluded.



	 



	RV Lot



	RVs are permitted to enter beginning at 8:00 AM (1) day prior to scheduled home games. Entry to the RV Lot is located off Southwestern Blvd. The RV Lot entry closes at 10:00 PM (1) day prior to scheduled home games. There is no day of game entry permitted for RVs.



	Vehicles are not permitted to exit and re-enter the RV Lot on game days.



	RVs are not permitted to depart from the RV Lot on the day of a game until (2) hours after the game has concluded. All RVs must depart from the RV Lot by 2:00 PM the day after the game.



	No parking or lining up early along Southwestern Blvd. is permitted. Spaces are guaranteed for permit holders.  Violator(s) may be subject to ticketing by local law enforcement and/or towed at owner's expense.



	No RV's or other vehicles will be permitted in any other parking areas and/or driveways outside of these published hours.  Vehicles that arrive during closed hours will not be admitted to the lot.



	Additional vehicles are not permitted in the RV Lot or allowed to park at the entrance to the RV Lot.  No guest vehicles are permitted in any of the Highmark Stadium lots.



	RV Lot parking permits are only valid for the RV and are not to be transferred to a car, truck or other vehicle that is not towing a RV.  If a car or truck shows with a RV Lot permit without towing a RV, they will be directed to a standard vehicle parking lots and will not need to purchase another permit.



	Parking team representatives will assist in the parking of vehicles to maximize availability in the lot.



	Vehicles must have proper spacing between them, both side to side and nose to tail.  Please be wary of parking RV's with open extensions into another RV's open extensions and leaving no access aisles for emergencies.  Vehicles must park according to the instructions of the lot attendants.



	The fire lanes must be kept clear.  The fire lane is clearly marked with yellow diagonal lines.



	Porta-johns are located in the Camper Lot for your convenience.  Please do not relocate them.



	The Town of Orchard Park prohibits open burning.



	There are no power supplies or septic services available for personal use.



	No golf carts, skateboards, bikes, or drones are allowed in the RV Lot.  All pets must be leashed.



	No weapons or fireworks of any kind are permitted.



	Please adhere to the Town of Orchard Park noise ordinance.  QUIET HOURS BEGIN AT 10:00 PM. Loud music/sound systems that are deemed offensive to others is not permitted.  Thank you for being courteous to fellow RV's.  Non-compliance is subject to ejection from the lot and/or loss of future parking privileges.



	 



	Tailgating



	Parking spaces consist of a 9ft by 18ft parking stall with a 9ft by 10ft tailgating area behind the parked vehicle. All tailgating activities must fit within this allotted space.



	All emergency lanes, drive aisles and crosshatched areas must always remain clear and unobstructed. Vehicle tailgates should not interfere with the flow of traffic. Emergency lanes must be kept clear of tailgating equipment to allow emergency response vehicles and personnel to pass through.



	Tailgating areas must be kept in a neat and orderly condition, and all trash must be disposed of in proper receptacles. Guests must return their area to its original state before entering the event. Trash bags must not be left beside a car or otherwise outside of a trash receptacle within the tailgating area.



	Tailgating in Highmark Stadium parking lots conclude at kickoff. At this time, all guests must enter the stadium with their game ticket.



	 



	Permitted Items



	Use of tents, so long as they do not encroach into the marked emergency vehicle lane or take space in adjacent parking spaces.



	Natural gas & propane grills



	Charcoal grills & open-fit fires that are raised at least 6 inches off the ground. Coals must be completely extinguished prior to entering the stadium and are not permitted to be dumped within Highmark Stadium parking lots.



	Plastic or non-breakable cups/cans



	Guests may bring and prepare food for consumption by their friends & family only.



	Personal-sized amplified sound system (e.g. small Bluetooth speaker)



	Bicycles are permitted in tailgating areas only at designated bike racks



	 



	Prohibited Items



	Stakes, through-surface inserts (e.g. tent poles), anything driven into the ground



	Charcoal grills & open-pit fires that are not raised at least 6 inches off the ground.



	Wood stoves, oil fryers and/or other cooking stations.



	Bottles, glass containers



	Sale of food or beverage and private catering companies.



	Electrical cords cannot be placed across parking areas/drive aisles or in areas that would create a hazard for any guests.



	Portable public address systems are not permitted. Amplified sound systems cannot be used at excessive volumes, and playing music with inappropriate language (profanity, slurs, etc.) is prohibited.



	Non-licensed motorized and non-motorized vehicles are prohibited within the designated tailgating parking lot(s), including without limitation golf carts, Segways, skateboards, scooters, and hoverboards.



	Drones, remote-controlled unmanned aerial vehicles or other similar motorized vehicles/devices; possession or operation of such devices may result in immediate ejection from the site and may also result in confiscation of such devices by security and law enforcement.



	Megaphones, airhorns, and other noise making devices



	Selling of items or soliciting of any promotional or marketing activities



	Any item deemed inappropriate or dangerous to spectators, participants or Team Members.



	Weapons or firearms – this extends to both real weapons and fake weapons such as toy guns, swords, knives, hatchets or bombs that might be part of a costume

stories.title: Jedi Council
stories.summary:
Mad at Ads and Short on Grit Issue is Back



Hello fellow DBTBers, just a little Jedi Council to hopefully brighten your day. A new article for you to digest as we near the end of July, 2026 already. The poor kids here in Florida go back to school in just three weeks. I remember somewhere around September 7th for the start of the school year in Buffalo. I would have dreaded having to go back to school in the middle of August.



So away we go with a few topics of interest to me and hopefully you as well.



1. Casinos and Ironman Sponsorship?



As you may have heard, the Buffalo Sabres have joined most of the NHL by adding corporate advertising to their home and away jerseys. Color me disappointed to see our hometown team finally succumb to the almighty dollar. It wasn’t unexpected, but it’s still a little disheartening. I liked being one of the last hold outs on that commercialization nonsense. It was a point of pride that their sweaters remained untouched. Unfortunately, that’s no longer the case.



Former NHL Chief Operating Officer John Collins first brought the concept to the forefront in 2014, arguing that uniform sponsorships were inevitable. Unfortunately, he was right. Ads on NHL jerseys first originated as a league-wide initiative proposed by NHL executives and approved by the Board of Governors in August 2021 to generate massive new revenue streams.



Five years later, only two NHL teams (the Dallas Stars and the San Jose Sharks) do not have corporate jersey ad sponsors heading into the 2026-27 season. All other 30 teams have active jersey patch agreements. The Sabres will feature Seneca Resort and Casino on their home uniforms and Stark Tech on their road duds. Both will be small patches on the upper left side of the hockey jersey. That is Stark TECH by the way, not Stark Industries. No Avengers will be affiliated with the organization, sorry Marvel fans. 



Another company, Stark Naked, was turned down for obvious reasons.



Every NHL team now features an advertisement on their helmet, and most fans don’t seem to mind. Ads on jerseys, however, are a different story. To many hockey purists, they’re a blemish on the traditional beauty of a team’s sweater. I’m firmly in that camp as well.



With that in mind, here’s what the Sabres are presenting us with.







I know some people around here are not fond of the gambling industry that has really infiltrated the sports world in the last ten years. So the Seneca Resort and Casino sponsorship will never be appreciated by some. Visually speaking, at least the patch is also royal blue like the jersey and the lettering and logo are only white. There is thankfully no color mismatch between the two. A few NHL clubs out there sport colors on their ads in contrast to their team colors and it’s a real eyesore.



As far as the Stark Tech sponsorship on the road uniforms, the logo appears a little smaller than the Seneca home patch. The wording is a darker blue than the Sabres’ royal blue but barely noticeable from a distance. There is also some faint light blue and light green in the logo but the smaller size makes it hard to see. All in all, it could have been a lot worse. Neither patch is jarringly offensive, and eventually we will learn to live with them. I’m still going to bitch about it though, every chance I get. I absolutely loath the whole cash grab of having ads on hockey jerseys.



But if it’s going to be forced upon us, at least ours isn’t too obnoxious or embarrassing. No Chico’s Bail Bonds to be had.



2. True Grit



The Sabres have enough players who are willing to compete, but this offseason has left them with a shortage of players who consistently make opponents pay physically. The team dealt away size, strength and toughness in Jordan Greenway and Alex Tuch and also lost physical scrapper Josh Dunne to free agency. Buffalo added the monstrous Louis Crevier on the backend but no enhancement has been made to the forward ranks to replace that grit.









For years, Buffalo was viewed as a team that could be pushed around. Management recognized that and made a point of adding heavier, more abrasive players to the bottom of the lineup. They specifically targeted players who would forecheck, finish checks, and make the team harder to play against. Along with an occasional bout thrown in when needed. Last season’s Sabres were a team based on speed but they could throw their weight around too and answer the bell when needed. On paper, this year’s team may be even faster, but they don’t have as much muscle up front anymore. I worry that will cost them eventually, with the ‘roid rage goons of Tampa, always physical Boston and the newly hulked up Panthers just waiting to take cheap shots at them.



The 4th line of Krebs, Malenstyn and Carrick have tenacity and willingness to use the body on their opponents. All three will stick up for teammates but none of them are known for being a true protector on the ice. Beck is tough hombre’ but Krebs and Carrick don’t have the size to match their spirit. If the gloves come off, I say a quick prayer that neither player is going to get hurt and miss 20 games. Krebs in particular has a pattern of barely hanging on in his fights.



So where am I going with this? I believe the team is short at least one more physical forward. Somebody who forechecks hard, hits harder and is willing to throw down at a moment’s notice. A physical, go-to player the other team is always wary off. But the Sabres could also use a top-six forward to help replace Alex Tuch’s production too. Or at least a good portion of it. It’s highly doubtful they can bring in a 60-65 point player at this stage of the summer. But what about a 45 point one who also fills the grit and toughness aspect I’ve been going on about?



Enter the idea for Buffalo to aquire Utah’s Lawson Crouse. (yes, I’m still on this player for like 4 years now) The Sabres would be killing two birds with one stone trading for the big winger. He has all the traits I’ve been talking about that Buffalo is now short on. Crouse is a premier physical forward in the NHL, standing 6-foot-4 and 215 pounds. He is known for policing the ice and protecting his teammates, while dishing out heavy hits along the way. He can forecheck hard and obviously handle himself in a fight. He is the perfect addition for what the team lacks.



Crouse is not without skill or offensive ability, though, and that’s where the “two-for-one” value of acquiring him comes into play. Lawson has scored 20 or more goals in four of the past five seasons. Last year, he found the back of the net 24 times while adding 20 assists for 44 points, all while posting an NHL career-best +20 rating. He’s not the offensive dynamo that some of the fantasy trade proposals involving Buffalo have envisioned over the past several months. Realistically, Crouse is probably a middle-six forward on most NHL teams. That said, I believe the Sabres could utilize him very effectively on their second line. Surrounded by Buffalo’s high-end offensive talent, there’s even a chance his production could take another step forward.









Where Crouse really separates himself, however, is with the intangibles. He would instantly inject a much needed dose of size, toughness, and physicality into Buffalo’s top six while also serving as a protector for the team’s skilled players. Adding a forward who can contribute offensively while filling that role would address two major needs with one acquisition.



Lawson is also a regular and significant contributor on the penalty-killing unit, an area depleted by the departure of Alex Tuch. He frequently averages nearly three minutes of ice time per game while shorthanded. 



The 29 year old’s current contract pays him an expected annual salary (AAV) of $4.3 million. His multi-year deal is set to expire at the end of the 2026-27 season, at which point he is scheduled to become an unrestricted free agent. His actual cap hit this year is only $3.9 million which the Sabres could easily finagle into the lineup. Any deal would likely involve Crouse signing an extension. I imagine he would be looking for something along the lines of $6-7 million per season and at least a five year deal which Buffalo could afford with extra cap space next year. He would be worth it in my opinion.



I feel most of us would like to add a goal scorer while also bringing in a banger to replace what we have lost. Crouse does that with one move from GMJK. I won’t speculate on what it would take to acquire him. Most trade ideas are shot down anyways as either too much or not enough to give up. If I’m the Sabres’ brass however, I’m considering what some goofy “writer” from this forum is pushing. Or even some intern named T. McGee. Buffalo has taken a hit this offseason both in toughness and offense. The young talent of Kulich, Ostlund and Helenius could certainly be a fill-in factor from within. But adding an experienced, physical forward and a proven goal scorer would add an extra layer of protection to the defending Atlantic Division Champions.



So will this actually come to fruition? Like most hopeful deals made by fans, probably not. Buffalo’s GM may be off parasailing right now or on his 5th cocktail in Aruba. But I feel that this move would address both problems the Sabres’ face amongst the forward ranks. To me, they are still short an experienced scoring forward and some overall heavy sandpaper. This would be a great option to fill both those needs.



If you made it this far, I hope everyone is enjoying their summer. The NHL regular season kicks off in only about 9 more weeks…

stories.title: Dion Dawkins loses 45 pounds
stories.summary:
Interesting that he was previously upset with fans for criticizing his weight, but glad he decided to do something about it. His weight certainly looked like a problem the last several years as he was getting beat in key moments, and even looking like he was taking plays off.
	 



	
		Quote
	

	
		
			Buffalo Bills offensive tackle Dion Dawkins is going to have a new look ahead of the 2026 NFL season.
		

		
			 
		

		
			Dawkins told USA TODAY's Ralphie Aversa at the 2026 ESPYs he was feeling "good" ahead of the upcoming season. The 32-year-old tackle acknowledged that was because of a key change he made for the campaign.
		

		
			 
		

		
			"I've told [everyone] in the world that this will be the lightest season that I ever play," Dawkins said.
		

		
			Dawkins was listed as weighing 320 pounds by the Bills during the 2025 NFL season. The 6-5 tackle acknowledged he had dropped 45 pounds since his peak, though it wasn't clear whether his peak was his listed weight.
		

		
			 
		

		
			What was Dawkins' goal in dropping that weight?
		

		
			"To play a little faster, play a little better because something is not getting us over that hump," Dawkins said. "So I want to be at the best that I could possibly be. So I said, (expletive) it, let's lose some weight."
		

		
			 
		

		
			Dawkins noted he was still confident in his athleticism playing at a heavier weight. Still, he thought changing things up could benefit the Bills as they seek the right combination to get the team to the Super Bowl for the first time since 1994.
		

		
			 
		

		
			"I am fast heavy," Dawkins explained, "but I might be just a little bit faster, lighter. And that might be what Josh [Allen] needs to get us over that hump."
		

		
			Of course, Dawkins also detailed that Allen hadn't yet seen him at the lighter weight.
		

		
			 
		

		
			"He'll probably see me and be like, 'All right, Dion, it's time to eat a little bit,'" Dawkins said. "But I would rather have that than all right Dion's time to lose a little bit. So I'd rather start super light and see how it goes."
		

		
			 
		

		
			The good news for the veteran tackle? First-year Bills coach Joe Brady is on board with his plan to drop weight.
		

		
			"If I come in lighter, I get a couple of the touchdown passes," Dawkins joked when asked about Brady. "So we'll see."

stories.title: Pop Quiz, Hotshot! 2025-26 Sabres Edition
stories.summary:
A Magical Season to Remember in Return to the Playoffs



Last season’s Buffalo Sabres sure was a wild ride. The year started like business as usual with Buffalo in the lower half of the league before bottoming out at one point. Then something clicked as the team took off and never looked back, inching out the Atlantic Division title over always tough Tampa Bay and upstart Montreal. That led to their first playoff appearance in forever, then a six game series win over Boston before eventually falling in seven games to the Habs. The Sabres were an OT win away from being in the final four. Just crazy to contemplate, even now.



As we all wait on a potential roster move/upgrade from Jarmo and the Sabres’ brass, put your thinking caps on and see how well you remember the events of this past season. Here is a ten question pop quiz, answer honest and see how you score. Just ten questions in total, good luck! The answer key is at the bottom.



1. Lightning Crashes



In the fight filled, high scoring 8-7 victory over Tampa Bay, which Buffalo players scored the late goal to tie it and the even later goal to win it?



A. Zucker and Dahlin B. Tuch and Dahlin C. Zucker and Doan D. Tuch and Doan



2. A Perfect 10



On December 31st, 2025, the Buffalo Sabres defeated the Dallas Stars 4-1. It was their 10th win in a row. Which Sabre scored two third period goals to cement the win?



A. Benson B. Tuch C. Ostlund D. Thompson



3. Plus Sized



Mattias Samuelsson had the best plus/minus on the team at +41. Who had the 2nd best plus/minus?



A. Tuch B. McLeod C. Benson D. Metsa



4. Zero Hour



How many shutouts did the Sabres record during the 2025-26 regular season?



A. Three B. Four C. Five D. Six



5. Take Your Shot



Back in March, the Sabres beat the Sharks 5-0 in San Jose with a minimal number of shots on goal. 5 goals on how many shots?



A. 10 B. 12 C. 14 D. 16



6. It’s All About the Percentages



Which Sabres’ defenseman had the highest shooting percentage among Buffalo defenders last season?



A. Samuelsson B. Byram C. Power D. Dahlin



7. Playoffs? You Kidding Me?



How many Buffalo players scored 10 or more points in their 13 game playoff run?



A. Two B. Three C. Four D. Five



8. He Shoots, He Scores!



What was the most goals scored in a single game by the Sabres during the 2025–26 NHL regular season?



A. Eight (once) B. Eight (twice) C. Nine D. Ten



9. Everybody Gonna Jump For Joy



Jack Quinn set a career high for goals, assists and points last season. How many points in total?



A. 45 B. 50 C. 51 D. 55



10. Three’s Company



Buffalo secured three wins against four divisional rivals this past season. Which one listed below is NOT one of those teams?



A. Toronto B. Boston C. Tampa D. Ottawa



That is a wrap, my friends. All done, you are! The answer key is below. How did you do?









Answer Key




The answer is C. Zucker tied it on a partial breakaway and Doan won it on the rebound after Dahlin hit the post.



The answer is D. TNT capped the game with 2 third period goals.



The answer is C. Benny was a +27 on the season. McLeod was +25 in third place.



The answer is C again. The Sabres had 5 shutouts with all three goalies chipping in. Lyon had three with UPL and Ellis notching one each.



The answer is D. Buffalo finished the game with 5 goals on just 16 shots.



The answer is A. Samuelsson was 11.9% (13 goals on 109 shots)



The answer is B. Three players scored at least 10 points. Thompson had 15 (5-10) Dahlin had 14 (4-10) and Doan had 10. (3-7)



The answer is C. Buffalo layeth the smack down on Chicago during a 9-3 win for their highest goal total of the year. They did score 8 goals twice though, against Tampa and Ottawa.



The answer is C. Quinn scored 51 points on the year. (20 goals, 31 assists)



The answer is D. The Sabres had three wins each against Toronto, Boston, Tampa and FLORIDA, not Ottawa.

stories.title: Peyton’s Place: Krebs Signs for Four More Years in Buffalo
stories.summary:
The 5th Year Sabre Had a Career High 39 Points Last Year



Well, that was a little more difficult than expected. And expensive from most points of view. Peyton Krebs had to file for arbitration in order to come to an agreement with Buffalo but thankfully the two sides settled today before that came to fruition. It was a long and challenging process though.



Peyton “Swiss army knife” Krebs has signed to remain in Buffalo for the next four years. The versatile forward finally joins Zach Benson and Beck Malenstyn (and Olen Zellweger) as recent Sabres’ RFAs who have inked a contact to remain with the Blue and Gold.



Peyton’s deal is officially for $4.5 million per season, substantially higher than most estimates. But the deal has more term than expected as well, which should balance some cost with the cap later. 



Krebs has stated publicly that his family loves it here and he wants too win a Cup in Buffalo. That is fine by me, and all of Sabres’ fandom I’m sure. Krebs is a valuable resource to have. He is not great at any one thing but is good at many. We saw more offense from him this past season than ever before. He plays sound defensively and wins many puck battles. He has a big heart on the ice, works his ass off and is an underrated leader for this team. He can play up and down the lineup and doesn’t look out of place. And he never backs down from adversity.









With Buffalo still in need of possible top-six help in the forward ranks, Krebs could still be a trade piece. Even moreso with the higher than expected contract and the difficult negotiations each side just had. The Sabres are heavy in the bottom-six and at least two forwards could be shipped out to make room for the bigger fish. If so, I hope Krebs is not one of them. Lindy and Jarmo seem to love the player also. He has great tenacity and spirit and willingness to battle. He, along with Josh Doan and Zach Benson, are the kind of players that Buffalo needs more of.



His price tag is certainly above expectations. Hopefully his output will be the same way.

stories.title: T McGee’s 2026 NHL Draft Post-Mortem & Peek at 2027
stories.summary:
DBTB –



Well, as I have said many times before, let no one claim that I am an unaccountable draftnik who throws out his rankings and then runs for cover, never to speak about it again!  I’ve always wanted to have the meteorologists (aka weathermen/ladies) get on TV and announce their accuracy percentages, although that will never happen.  But given my situation here at DBTB, I wanted to walk the walk and talk the talk.  Or insert favorite cliché here.  So here it is, my accuracy metrics for 2026!  



This was a tough year for me.  The success of the Sabres had me more focused on the Blue and Gold than I had been in a while.  That left me less time to focus on the Draft than normal, and that’s reflected in my relatively poor performance as far as predicting things.  Granted, it wasn’t SO far off previous years, but it was off, for the most part.  So mea culpa, mea culpa!      



I know due to a lot of logistical snafus, you all didn’t get to see my final Mock Draft.  For the three of you that care.  But, just to be clear, I did finish my Mock Draft on the Monday before the Draft.  So I was unable to take into account some major events:  not the Brady Tkachuk deal, the Will Eklund trade, nor the Bowen Byram trade or the Pavel Dorofeyev deal.  Some moves that had a pretty big impact on how parts of the Draft went down, honestly. 



Not an excuse, but I would’ve done the Draft a bit differently had I been able to take those deals into account.  I might have gotten 2-3 more selections correct had those deals come down a few days earlier.  Let me emphasize, MIGHT. 



Here we go.  This is how I did for each round in terms of accuracy.  This is not exact slots, but rather a player that went off the Board in the Round in which I had him going.  So I did not have Ilia Morozov going at #20, but I did get him going in Round 1, so that’s one right for me.  Just to beclear about how the scorekeeping went.    



Round 1: 



I finished with 25 of 32, which is pretty low for me.  Usually, I’m up around 27-28 right out of 32 for the first round.  But the bunch in the late 1st through the mid 2nd made it tough to pick and choose.  As far as the Sabres go, I had Rudolph at #11 in my Mock Draft, and Morozov at #16.  I had 5 defenders go off the Board before I had Rudolph getting chosen.  Not a great start for me.



Round 2: 



I did about standard for the 2nd.  Got 11 of 31 (remember, Vegas had to forfeit their 2nd round draft pick due to some silliness with Tortorella and the media) right.  Will admit I was surprised by a couple of players that I had for sure going as high as the late 1st that didn’t go in the 2nd.  Again, a little below my normal number, but not far off. 



Round 3:



Things picked up a little here as I got 10 of 32.  Typically, the 3rd is when I start to fall off, but I stayed pretty close to the 2nd round, which doesn’t always happen.  And I just missed on a couple guys that went at the end of the 2nd, and a couple more that went at the beginning of the 4th.  Could have easily finished with half (16) right! 



Round 4: 



Speaking of the 4th, this is where things start to go off the rails.  And no different this year, as I only managed 7 of 32 in this round.  Interestingly, I had Sabres’ selection Olivier Murnieks going at #123 overall, just one spot off from where the Sabres actually chose him.  I was close on that one at least!



Round 5: 



A decent showing here with 6 of 32, which is especially gratifying since this was the first round of the Draft where multiple guys I didn’t have on my Board started appearing. Guys who I had either removed during the year or never even made it on to my radar got selected in the 5th round.  As for the Sabres, their 5th round selection – Doman Szongoth – I did not have getting chosen until the 7th round.  So a miss for me there! 



Round 6:



Predictably, I went miserable 3 for 32 in this round.  I was surprised to see a number of players that I had much higher go in the 6th. Unfortunately for me, the Sabres choice, Dylan Dumont, was not in my Top 200 and I can’t even remember watching him this season.  Supposedly, he grew a few inches during the year.  Drummondville, where Dumont played, had one goaltender that I caught a couple of times this year, and another late riser in Louis-Felix Bourque (who went in the 3rd round, where I had him going!).  Somehow I just flat-out missed Dumont. 



Round 7: 



Last but not least, I managed a meager 2 of 32 in the 7th round.  I did have Sabres’ development camp invite Cohen Bidgood going in the middle of the 7th round, so I imagine they would’ve taken him if they had a selection in the 7th.  Always the toughest round to predict, my rather sub-par year for 2026 culminated in a pretty bleak 7th round showing.  In 2025, I think I managed to get 5 or 6 right in the 7th round but really struggled in rounds 4-5-6.  So I guess it all balanced out in the end. 



What this should tell you all is that I barely know what I’m talking about!  But I want to thank Calvin, Melissa, Chad, Jedi, and all the DBTB brain trust for giving me a platform to post my draft and prospect blathering for another year.  Even a year when our beloved Sabres didn’t care much for the Draft, prospects, or anything other than beating the brakes off Boston and almost squashing Montreal. 



As always, feel free to ping me anytime with any questions or comments about the Draft, Sabre prospects, or my (putrid) performance as a prognosticator. 



As you know, the cycle that supplies the NHL with an ever-growing pot of talent never stops. So I’ll offer you a quick Watch List for next season, which looks to have some really strong forwards at the top of the Draft (unlike this past year, which really had the blueliners dominating), including a few potential #1 centermen…which always makes a Draft stand out. This is in no particular order, just my Top 32 at this moment in time:

1. 60+ yard field goals = 4 points
	2.  One foot in bounds = catch
	3. Red zone penalties revert to half the distance to the goal. 
	4. The "Tush Push" is eliminated.
	5. No punting inside the opponent’s 50-yard line.
	6. Overtime: 3 alternating attempts per team from the 5 yard line.
	 
	7. Point aftertouchdown options:
	- 1 point – Kick from the 33-yard line
	- 2 points – Ball on the 2-yard line
	- 3 points – Ball on the 8-yard line
